Morocco Issues Orange Alert for Thunderstorms, Hail Risk Across Several Provinces
Morocco’s meteorological service has issued an orange-level weather alert for several provinces, warning of thunderstorms, possible hail and strong wind gusts expected on Saturday and Sunday.
Agadir – Morocco’s General Directorate of Meteorology (DGM) has forecast thunderstorms accompanied by possible hail and strong wind gusts in several provinces on Saturday and Sunday, issuing an orange-level weather alert.
The storms could bring rainfall of 20 to 30 millimeters on Saturday and between 20 and 40 mm on Sunday, according to the DGM’s weather warning.
On Saturday, thunderstorms are expected from 2 p.m. until midnight in Azilal, Oujda-Angad, Jerada, Taourirt, Guercif, Beni Mellal and Taza.
The weather conditions could persist into Sunday, when the DGM expects thunderstorms in a wider group of provinces. The warning will cover Zagora, Figuig, Azilal, Errachidia, Midelt, Boulemane, Chefchaouen, Fahs-Anjra, Mdiq-Fnideq, Tinghir, Al Haouz and Tetouan.
The forecast places Sunday’s warning period between 10 a.m. and midnight, with expected rainfall ranging from 20 to 40 mm. The DGM also warned of possible hail and wind gusts accompanying the storms.
The orange vigilance level signals potentially hazardous weather conditions that may affect daily activities, particularly in areas exposed to intense rainfall, hail and strong winds.
Residents in the affected provinces should follow official weather updates and take precautions during the alert periods. Drivers should also remain cautious in areas experiencing heavy rainfall, as wet roads and reduced visibility can make travel more difficult.
The DGM’s warning covers specific periods on both days, with the forecast indicating that several provinces could experience thunderstorms through Saturday evening and Sunday night.

Beed, Oct 17 (PTI) Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Ajit Pawar on Saturday reviewed the severe drought conditions in Beed district, and directed the district administration to execute relief measures on a war footing.
Presiding over a high-level review meeting at the Beed Collectorate, she assessed the prevailing water scarcity, crop damage and fodder shortages across the district.
MLAs Prakash Solanke and Dhananjay Munde, Collector Vivek Johnson, Zilla Parishad Chief Executive Officer Jithin Rahman, Superintendent of Police Navneet Kanwat and other officials took part in the meeting chaired by Pawar, who is also the guardian minister of Beed.
As rain deficit has triggered acute shortage of drinking water and fodder, Pawar instructed the officials to expedite crop loss assessments.
Prioritising drinking water management, Pawar mandated GPS-enabled tracking for all operational water tankers to ensure accountable and timely distribution. The district currently deploys 225 water tankers to scarcity-hit pockets.
She reiterated that potable water must strictly not be diverted for construction activities and appealed for judicious use of water.
She also directed the authorities to immediately undertake water conservation works, including desilting and deepening rivers and nullahs, groundwater recharge, and repairing public wells.
To counter imminent fodder shortages, Pawar asked the administration to deploy forward planning by training farmers in silage, hydroponics, and azolla cultivation.
She directed that employment guarantee works under government schemes be integrated directly with water conservation projects to provide guaranteed local livelihoods and prevent distress migration from rural belts.
Given the crisis, the guardian minister appealed to citizens to practice restraint by curbing non-essential expenditures on weddings and birthdays, encouraging mass marriage ceremonies instead.
Pawar issued strict directions ordering all departmental officers and field staff to remain stationed at their respective headquarters to assist the public.
Emphasising the human dimension of the crisis, she instructed field teams to step up proactive outreach, counselling, and emotional support for distressed farmers.
“The state government and administration stand firmly behind our citizens in this hour of crisis. We are operating at peak capacity across all fronts to ensure comprehensive relief and pull our farming community safely through this natural calamity,” Pawar said.
The state government has declared 305 out of the total 358 talukas as drought-hit. PTI COR NP

A yellow alert has been issued in Ukraine
A yellow alert has been issued in four regions of Ukraine due to thick fog. Drivers and pedestrians should be especially careful due to reduced visibility.
“In the coming hour and continuing through the first half of the day on October 17, fog will cover the city of Kyiv, and during the night and morning of October 18, it will affect the Vinnytsia, Kirovohrad, Cherkasy, and Kyiv regions,” rescue workers warn.
According to them, visibility during this period will range from 200 to 500 meters.
The State Emergency Service of Ukraine announced that a Level I (yellow) hazard alert has been issued.
Against this backdrop, emergency responders also reminded the public that reduced visibility could complicate traffic conditions.
“We urge drivers to maintain a safe speed, keep a safe distance, and turn on their fog lights, and we urge pedestrians to be sure to wear reflective gear and be careful at crosswalks. Stay safe and be mindful of weather conditions,” the rescue workers concluded.
Source: State Emergency Service
Rain, fog, and a cold snap are forecast for Ukraine on October 17.
As a reminder, rainy weather will persist in most regions of Ukraine in the coming days.
